title: Nobody Works Alone
subtitle: Operation Magpie
story:
Sixty jobs in three years, and not one of them forced. The Service does not care who owns the stones; it cares that somebody has learned to move them, and that nobody can say how many somebodies that is. One report says a single crew with a long reach. Another says the city is thick with them. You and your partner have until the tide turns to settle it.

You will work the case from opposite ends. One of you takes the front door and the scenes themselves — how each place was entered, with what, and for how long. The other takes the back door and the disposal — what left each place, where it surfaced, and through whose hands. Neither half answers the question on its own. When you each have your count, meet aboard the Aurelia before the party ends, and bring everything you picked up on the way.

done.title: The count is made
done.body: You have your number and your partner has theirs, and they are not the same number. Neither of you has made a mistake. That is the finding.

escapeDone.title: Five hands, three tables
escapeDone.body: Seated, the room reads at a glance: two houses running two crews apiece, and one man who answers to nobody. The count was never one number. It was a question about how far down you were willing to look.

debrief.title: How the count worked
debrief.intro: This world was built to argue one thing: that k is not a property of your data. It is a property of the question you asked of it. You and your partner clustered the same eleven burglaries and got different numbers because you asked different questions of them — and both answers were true.

worldPlatePrompt: A world-bible establishing plate: ONE single continuous interior, a single unbroken photographic frame — NOT a grid, NOT a montage, NOT a contact sheet, NOT panels or tiles. The grand ground-floor lobby of a private members' club in a modern European city, late at night, looking across it in one view. Cold white marble floor and columns give way to deep walnut panelling and oxblood buttoned leather; a long bar of dark wood and tarnished gilt runs down one side, ranked cut-crystal glassware catching the light; a green baize card table stands beyond it; brushed-steel and glass doors at the far end open onto wet black tarmac and a single cold neon sign in the street outside. Deep blue-black shadow throughout with warm sodium and amber pooling from low lamps, one cold accent from the doorway. Cigarette haze in the air. Painterly, cinematic, high contrast, film grain. TIME-NEUTRAL — soft even light, neither dawn nor dusk, so each room's own prompt drives its hour. No people, no figures, no lettering, no captions, no text, no signage, no numbers.
coverPrompt: Minimalist stylised thumbnail poster, square: the bold dark silhouette of a single magpie perched on the rim of an open jewellery case, one amber glow rising from inside the case and throwing the bird into hard relief. Deep blue-black ground. No people, no lettering, no text. Must read at thumbnail size.

_designNotes.twoPlayer: EXPERIMENTAL. Two students, two browsers, one dataset, two feature blocks. A clusters the entry block into 5 teams; B clusters the disposal block into 3 organisations; the truth is 5 nested inside 3, split 2+2+1. Coordination is verbal only — nothing is synced.
_designNotes.escapeTier: TIER 2 by deliberate exception — connected to the puzzles but NOT driven by their data. The world confirms the numbers; no dataset value crosses into the escape. Documented in notes.md so an audit does not flag it against the data-free-meta-echo rule.
_designNotes.register: Bond by INTERIORS AND HOURS, never by climate. The corpus is saturated with cold and hawaii already claims tropical. Urban/modern/clinical is this scenario's own claimed ground.
_designNotes.softGate: Role choice is a soft gate — gameState resets on reload. Accepted; a student would be doing twice the work to avoid a conversation, and the codec records their path.

rooms.title: The Royal Box
rooms.designNote:
RUNG 1 (A) — assign a case to a group.
WHY THEY ARE HERE: This is TONIGHT'S job — the twelfth. During the second act the contents of a private box's wall safe went; nothing forced. A servant found it in the interval and it was kept quiet so the house would not empty, which is why the performance is still running below. The agent has until the curtain.
THE QUESTION IN THE ROOM: Does tonight belong to the file at all, or is this a copycat?
ANALYSIS: Cluster the entry evidence across all twelve jobs and find which group tonight's falls into.
VERIFIED ANSWER = 18. kmeans(scale(case_file[,c('entry_height_m','tool_score','approach_min','entry_hour')]), 5, nstart=50); table(cluster) -> 18/13/11/10/8. Busiest crew = 18, runner-up 13 (+38%). Distractors: 13, 11, 10, 8, 29, 60.
SUPERSEDED-SPEC: ANSWER = the hand that did tonight's job.
THE JOB: **Thalberg Opera House** (row in case_file.csv — crew 1, tool_score 7.1, entry_height 0.4 m). ART CONTRACT FROM THE DATA: forced entry at ground level, heavy tool marks, visible damage. TOKEN 1 of 5 = crew 1's monogrammed lighter — the only token with a crisp marque.
WHAT THEY FIND: TOKEN 1 of 5 — a monogrammed lighter on the velvet seat, dropped by that crew. The ONLY token with a crisp house marque; it teaches the player what a legible mark looks like, so the ambiguity of the other four reads as ambiguity rather than as bad art.
WHAT IT CAUSES (why they leave): That same hand also did the Belgrave Mews job three weeks ago, which the file lumps into the same series and which was never properly worked. Go and confirm it.

ART: new. Mid-performance is diegetic, not decorative.

rooms.debrief: The plainest thing k-means does: given groups, say which one a case belongs to. You had no labels, no key, and no idea yet how many groups there were — only the geometry of the entry measurements. That is clustering doing its actual job, assigning by resemblance.

rooms.title: The Mayfair Townhouse
rooms.designNote:
RUNG 2 (A) — THE ELBOW. This is A's half of the scenario's central divergence.
WHY THEY ARE HERE: The unworked scene from room 1's answer. They arrive expecting to confirm ONE crew.
THE QUESTION IN THE ROOM: The house refuses that expectation: it carries two distinct sets of marks, left on two different occasions. So the question escalates from 'which crew did this one' to 'how many crews are there at all?'
ANALYSIS: The elbow. Cluster the entry block over all twelve jobs and read k off the plot.
VERIFIED ANSWER = k=5. WSS k=1..8 = 236/126/61/23/5/4/4/3 — the drop collapses after 5 (ratio 0.03). PICK-THE-POINT, not MCQ. B's elbow is k=3 on the same 60 jobs. Both correct.
SUPERSEDED-SPEC: ANSWER = 5 crews. B's elbow lands on 3 organisations. BOTH ARE RIGHT — 5 nested inside 3, split 2+2+1. Never 'fix' the divergence; it is the scenario.
THE JOB: **Belgrave Mews** (crew 2, tool_score 2.7, entry_height 7.6 m). ART CONTRACT: entry at an UPPER window, a climb, almost no tool damage — visibly unlike the opera's forced ground-floor entry. TOKEN 2 of 5 = crew 2's bone-coloured chip. Plus the valuer's card (the name B needs).
WHAT THEY FIND: TOKENS 2 and 3 of 5 — a bone-coloured chip (no crest, only a fleur-de-lis pressed into the rim) and a hotel key fob (a number and a colour, no house name). TWO tokens here BECAUSE two crews hit this house: the objects ARE the evidence that forces the room's question. ALSO the mid-point trade: a discreet VALUER'S CARD slipped behind the mirror — the sort a household keeps for appraisals. The name means nothing to A, who can only read it aloud; that valuer runs the casino's private room, so B cannot get in without it.
WHAT IT CAUSES (why they leave): The file said same series; the marks say otherwise — a different hand entirely. So the question is no longer which crew did this one, but HOW MANY crews are there. That is the elbow, and the room forced it.

ART: new.

VERIFIED ANSWER = 10. Summarise by cluster: crew 4 went in highest (mean entry height 9.77 m vs 7.69 m, +27%); report its SIZE = 10 jobs. Distinct entity from rungs 1 and boss.

THE JOB: **Harkness Gallery** (crew 4, entry_height 9.0 m — the HIGHEST in the file). ART CONTRACT: entry through the glazed barrel roof; the roof is load-bearing, not decoration. rooms.debrief: Summarising by cluster is what makes a cluster mean something. A group number is arbitrary until you ask what its members have in common — here, that one crew goes in higher than any other. Clusters become findings only when you describe them.

rooms.title: The Vault at First Light
rooms.designNote:
BOSS (A) — the scaling trap. A SOLO rung: it has a right answer and a named decoy, so the two-player divergence stays at the elbow, not here.
WHY THEY ARE HERE: The strongroom was hit last week — the largest haul of the twelve, still unattributed.
THE QUESTION IN THE ROOM: Which hand did the strongroom?
ANALYSIS: Haul value runs to thousands while every MO feature sits on a small scale. Cluster raw and you group by HOW MUCH was taken; scale first and you group by HOW IT WAS DONE. DECOY = the unscaled haul-band mate — the job that stole a similar amount, i.e. the mistake a real investigator would make.
VERIFIED ANSWER = Garsington Row. DECOY = Ashcombe Villa (Ardsley's raw duration-band mate — what you get without scale()). OPTIONS: Aldwick Court, Ashcombe Villa, Beckington Hall, Belgrave Mews, Bramfield Place, Garsington Row. Exactly one true hand-mate among the six. CLUE: minutes_inside runs to hundreds while every other entry feature is single digits — scale first.
SUPERSEDED-SPEC: ANSWER = the crew that did the strongroom.
THE JOB: **Ardsley Strongroom** (crew 5, tool_score 0.9 — the LOWEST in the file; haul_value 95,000, the largest). ART CONTRACT: NO forced entry anywhere. Nothing prised, nothing broken; the circular door stands open on its lugs, undamaged. The data says they were let in, so the art must not show a break-in. TOKEN 5 of 5 = crew 5's luggage tag.
WHAT THEY FIND: TOKEN 5 of 5 — a leather luggage tag, its routing stamp only partly legible. This completes the set: FIVE tokens for FIVE crews, one each, every one found at a scene that crew actually hit. The count is never asserted — it accumulates in the player's pocket and independently confirms their elbow.
WHAT IT CAUSES (why they leave): The routing stamp points at a vessel, and a gala invitation sits by the keypad.

SPECTACLE ROOM. ART: new.

rooms.title: The Gala at Sunrise
rooms.designNote:
SHARED FINALE + ESCAPE. Reached only when BOTH players have solved their boss and traded codes.
ENGINE: a `grid` (items x buckets) — NOT a `lock`. Emitting it as a lock is a named silent killer.
THE BOARD: five token cards along the foot of a brass-framed seating plan; three named tables ruled across it. Pin each crew's token to the table of the house that moves its goods.
HOW IT IS SOLVED — the mark, not the object. Each of the three houses is known by ONE MARK, shown in that house's own room on B's route: the bone house stamps no crest and presses a small FLEUR-DE-LIS; the marque house strikes its MARQUE on everything; the range house marks nothing but NUMBERS everything inside one narrow band. Each of A's five tokens CARRIES exactly one of those three marks. So the board is not object-matching — it is mark-matching, and the marks live on opposite sides of the pair.
WHY NEITHER CAN DO IT ALONE. A holds the objects and can describe every mark but has never seen a house, so a fleur-de-lis means nothing to them; only the lighter's complete marque is placeable unaided, and it exists to teach A what a legible mark looks like. B has stood in all three houses and knows every convention but has never seen a token. The exchange is therefore A DESCRIBING a physical mark in plain language and B IDENTIFYING it — which is the communication task the whole scenario is built to force.
SOLUTION (verified, _scratch/verify_escape.py, brute force over all 243 seatings -> exactly ONE): marque house = lighter + luggage tag; bone house = bone chip + book of matches; range house = key fob. 2+2+1, echoing the crews' nesting without carrying a single value out of the CSV.
NON-REDUNDANT: every token is placed by its OWN mark, never by elimination.
THE DECOY: sorting by what the objects ARE rather than what is stamped on them — smoking (lighter, matches), gaming (chip, fob), travel (tag) — gives a DIFFERENT partition of the SAME 2+2+1 shape. A wrong answer that looks right because it has the shape you expected, which is this scenario's own lesson re-posed on props.
ART CONTRACT (binding, both sides): each of B's three rooms must VISIBLY DISPLAY its house's mark — the fleur-de-lis stamp in the pawnbroker's ledger, the brass marque above the cage, the numbered tallies on the consignment board. Each of A's five tokens must carry its mark legibly AT CLOSE RANGE, with only the lighter's complete. Five generic tokens, or five fully-legible ones, break the escape.
NEVER label the slots 'organisations' and the cards 'crews' — that announces the nesting before the pair earn it. Five cards, three tables, no stated relationship. SPECTACLE ROOM. ART: new. SHARED.

rooms.debrief: The lesson made physical. Five cards, three tables, and the arithmetic refusing to come out even — because k was never a property of the data. It was a property of the question each of you asked of it. And the tempting wrong seating, sorting the tokens by what they ARE instead of by what is stamped on them, is the scaling trap again with no numbers in it at all: group on the wrong feature and you get a wrong answer in exactly the right shape.
